title: Senior asks: row 1 has keys id, fruit. Row 2 has the keys in another order. What does CsvFileActions::write() save for rows 1 and 2?
options: An error: different keys than row 1
explain: getRowValues() loops over the header names from row 1 and reads each value by key. The order inside row 2 does not matter. It throws only when the set of keys differs. This is why a row never ends up in the wrong column.

title: Senior asks: the URL has ?file=%20fruits.csv%20 (with spaces). What does getFileName() give, and what about ?file=%20%20?
explain: getRequired() trims the value first. So ' fruits.csv ' becomes 'fruits.csv' and then basename() runs. A value with only spaces is empty after trim, so the code throws InvalidRequestException (400). Trim before you check for empty. Otherwise ' ' would pass.

title: Senior asks: another website runs fetch('http://your-api/?action=write&file=a.csv', {method: 'POST', body: '[]', mode: 'no-cors'}). Your API sends no CORS headers. What happens?
options: The browser blocks it, PHP never runs
The request is sent and PHP writes the file. Only reading the answer is blocked
PHP refuses it because the Origin header is different
It works only if the user is logged in
explain: CORS controls who can read the answer, not who can send. A POST with a text/plain body is a 'simple request', so the browser sends it without a preflight. Your write action runs. Delete is safer by accident: DELETE needs a preflight. Fix: require an auth token or CSRF token, or require Content-Type: application/json.

pr.title: Add a FileName value object
pr.author: olha
pr.body: basename() is repeated in three places. This class checks the name once. The next PR will use it in FileService.

explain: Good PR. It is small, it only adds a class, and the object cannot be wrong after it is created. A readonly class makes the value fixed. basename() cannot change the name silently anymore. A name like ../x is refused with an error. Next step: use it in the controller and service, and add a test.

title: PHP 8. What does this print?
options: Fatal error on the first line
explain: ?-> stops the chain when the left side is null and the whole expression becomes null. No warning, no error. ?? then gives 'unknown' for the first line. var_dump shows NULL. Without ?->, reading ->city on null gives a warning and null in PHP 8.

title: What does Node print?
explain: const protects the variable, not the object inside. Changing user.name is allowed. Assigning a new object to user throws TypeError (Assignment to constant variable). So the output is TypeError, then Bob. Use Object.freeze() if the object itself must not change.

title: You ran git reset --hard HEAD~1 by mistake. Your last commit was not pushed and is gone from git log. Which command helps you find it?
explain: git reflog lists where HEAD pointed in the past, including the commit you just reset away. Copy its hash and run git reset --hard <hash> (or git branch rescue <hash>). The commit stays for weeks until garbage collection. git log does not show it because no branch points to it.

pr.title: Add POST /products
pr.author: copilot-fan
pr.body: Copilot wrote the controller. It saves name and price from the request.

explain: Nothing checks the input. A missing name gives null and a 500 error. The price 'abc' becomes 0.0 and a negative price is saved. A JSON body is not even read by request->request. Use a DTO with #[MapRequestPayload] and Assert rules. Symfony then returns 422 for bad data before your code runs.
